proposal: Before declaring a STANDARD/established technique "dead" or "doesn't work," do a quick literature check (WebSearch/arxiv) for the canonical working version — a failed local implementation falsifies the IMPLEMENTATION, not the TECHNIQUE. Day-135 instance: I buried the segmentation/perception-decoupling route for Anakin after one crude RGB-threshold mask FALSIFIED; an afternoon lit-check found the field's proven version (PencilNet: edge/pencil-filter → gate-pose, zero-shot sim-to-real) differs in EXACTLY the two axes I got wrong (edge-invariance not color, decoupled perception→pose not end-to-end). The 30-minute search would have reframed the whole morning's route work. Trigger: any time I write "X is dead / X doesn't work / abandon X" about a named, established method — pause and search for the working version first. Cheap insurance against burying a good technique on a bad implementation.
